# Workarounds for the Copy-Fail Linux kernel bug (CVE-2026-31431)

## Overview

This is a collection of workarounds for the local priviledge escalation bug in the Linux kernel.

**⚠️ Important Note:** Most content in this directory is **generated by GitHub Copilot and Claude**, outside of business hours. This includes code samples, documentation, and various text files that were created or assisted by AI but were tested by a human 💁‍♂️


## RPMs Provided

`make rpm-build` will build the following RPMs:
- **block-af-alg** - workaround for the original [copyfail](https://github.com/theori-io/copy-fail-CVE-2026-31431/tree/main) 0day by blocking the AF_ALG socket type.
- **block-udp-encap** - workaround for the [copyfail2 0day](https://github.com/0xdeadbeefnetwork/Copy_Fail2-Electric_Boogaloo) by blocking the UDP_ENCAP option to the setsockopt() calls.
## Files Provided

- **Makefile** — Automates compilation and installation. `make rpm-setup rpm-build` will give you installable RPMs on RHEL-like systems.
- **QUICK-REFERENCE.md** — Quick usage and troubleshooting reference.
- **RHEL9-AF-ALG-SETUP.md** — Full setup guide for RHEL9.
- **RPM-BUILD.md** — RPM packaging and build instructions.
- **block-af-alg.py** — BCC Python wrapper (easiest to use).
- **block_af_alg.c** — Standalone eBPF C source (can compile directly).
- **block-af-alg.service** — systemd service unit for loading the workaround on boot.
- **block-af-alg.spec** — RPM spec file for building the package.
- **block-udp-encap.service** — systemd service unit for loading the UDP encap workaround on boot.
- **block-udp-encap.spec** — RPM spec file for building the UDP encap package.
- **block_udp_encap.c** — Standalone eBPF C source for UDP encap (can compile directly).
- **lsm_loader.c** — C eBPF program loader for deployment without bpftools.
- **copy-fail-repro.py** — Re-formatted PoC script for the copy-fail bug.
- **copy-fail-workaround.yml** - Ansible playbook for the bootloader workaround (requires a reboot).


## ⚠️ Implication of disabling the AF_ALG socket type

AF_ALG is the "Address Family for Kernel Algorithms." It provides a user-space interface to the Linux Kernel Crypto API. Instead of using a library like OpenSSL to do the math on the CPU, an application can offload the work to the kernel.

Disabling this means your application will no longer able to use the kernel API and application that requires that will either stop working or run with performance degradation.
